question: Should OpenClaw core permanently support ordered configuration-authority layers with first-declaration path ownership and special monotonic tool-policy composition?
rationale: This creates a new CLI and configuration contract with security-boundary and upgrade implications; repository policy requires explicit maintainer discussion and acceptance for that direction.

options.title: Review the narrowed V1
options.body: Keep the RFC draft while maintainers evaluate the startup-only contract together with the open implementation and real lifecycle proof.

options.title: Revise the authority model
options.body: Keep the proposal open but change ordering, conflict, policy-tightening, or extension semantics before implementation lands.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Close the proposal and retain host-side effective-config generation if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to own multi-source authority semantics.

recommendation.title: Review the narrowed V1
recommendation.body: Keep the RFC draft while maintainers evaluate the startup-only contract together with the open implementation and real lifecycle proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline explicitly routes the repository-level product decision to this reviewer, while `giodl73-repo` remains the strongest implementation-context owner.
